title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Alipurduar and Cooch Behar Districts and adjoining areas in the State of West Bengal under West Bengal LSA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Alipurduar and Cooch Behar Districts and adjoining areas in the State of West Bengal under West Bengal LSA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 3:38PM by PIB Delhi The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Alipurduar and Cooch Behar Districts and adjoining areas in the State of West Bengal under West Bengal LSA, during the month of June 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services. These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems. TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 494.5 KMs, Hotspot locations - 16, Walk Test – 3.8 KMs in West Bengal State during 9 th June 2026 to 13 th June 2026 in West Bengal LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Kolkata. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test. Drive Test Route Map : The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating C ity drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots and Walk tests, as per the legends shown on the map: - Key Parameters Assessed Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G). Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS). Call Silence Instance : Number of call silence instance occurred during the calls. Data Services: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate The overall mobile network performance in Alipurduar and Cooch Behar Districts and adjoining areas for the key parameters has been summarised below: - a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the city drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 2771 / 64500 for Airtel , 21699 / 59947 for BSNL , 3101 / 60695 for RJIL and 10964 / 64434 for VIL . Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed . b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/ 453 for Airtel , 26 / 424 for BSNL , 3 / 457 for RJIL and 5 / 450 for VIL . Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map A nnexed . c) Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 19 / 446 for Airtel , 5 / 352 for BSNL , 10 / 443 for RJIL and 27 / 389 for VIL . Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed . d) Data Download and Upload Throughput : i) Data Download performance (Overall) : Average download speed was observed as 78.63  Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G) , 11.81 Mbps for BSNL (4G/2G) , 154.29 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 22.98 Mbps for VIL (4G/2G) . Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed. ii) Data Upload performance (Overall) : Average upload speed was observed as 18.05 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G) , 5.23 Mbps for BSNL (4G/ 2G) , 15.59 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 11.77 Mbps for VIL (4G/2G) . Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed. Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed. Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under: - a) City - The areas covered in the city drive are Birpara, Hasimara, Kalchini, Alipurduar, Rasikbil, Tufanganj, Balarampur, Dinhata, Kamtapur, Sitai, Sitalkuchi, Mathabhanga, Ghoksadanga, Falakat etc in Cities & adjoining areas of Alipurduar and Cooch Behar Districts.. b) Hotspot - The hot spot locations, capturing stationary user experience, are (i) Alipurduar Bus Stand Alipurduar; (ii) Alipurduar District Hospital - Hospital Road Alipurduar; (iii) Alipurduar Post Office (Mukhya Dak Ghar) 362 Station Road Sobhaganj; (iv) Alipurduar University Sobhaganj; (v) Buxa Tiger Reserve Forest SH12A Rajabhat Khawa; (vi) Cooch Behar Government Engineering College Post Ghughumari Harinchawra; (vii) Cooch Behar Head Post Office Sunity Road Cooch Behar; (viii) Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma University Shankar Mandal Road; (ix) Cooch Behar Royal Palace Bus Terminus Keshab Road; (x) Dooars Kanya District Government Office Alipurduar; (xi) Jaldapara National Park Jaldapara Uttar Madarihat; (xii) Kamakhyaguri Railway Station; (xiii) Madan Mohan Temple Cooch Behar; (xiv) Mathabhanga College Siliguri Road Khaterbari; (xv) Sitalkuchi BDO Office Sitai Road Sitalkuchi; (xvi) Tufanganj Hospital Tufanganj. c) Walk Test - The walk tests conducted during 9 th to 13 th June 2026, are (i) Cooch Behar Govt. Medical College Shankar Mandal Road; (ii) District Court of Alipurduar, New Administrative Building Alipurduar; (iii) New Alipurduar Railway Station; (iv) New Cooch Behar Junction Railway Station Gosanimari Cooch Behar, capturing mobile network behaviour in crowded pedestrian environments. The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to adv.kolkata@trai.gov.in or Regional Office of TRAI at Kolkata RO can be contacted on telephone no. +91-33-22361401 . Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems. TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 244.2 KMs, Hotspot locations - 9, Walk Test – 1.6 KMs in Tripura State during 13 th May 2026 to 16 th May 2026 in North East LSA. Data Services: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate The overall mobile network performance in South Tripura District and adjoining areas for the key parameters has been summarised below: - a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the city drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 6217 / 30754 for Airtel , 11854 / 28800 for BSNL , 7590/ 35527 for RJIL and 8627 / 19553 for VIL . Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed . d) Data Download and Upload Throughput : i) Data Download performance (Overall) : Average download speed was observed as 88.67  Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G) , 10.64 Mbps for BSNL (4G/2G) , 46.11 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 35.19 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G) . Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed. ii) Data Upload performance (Overall) : Average upload speed was observed as 17.32 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G) , 3.25 Mbps for BSNL (4G/ 2G) , 3.83 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 6.84 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G) . Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed. Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed. Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under: - a) City - The areas covered in the city drive Rajnagar, Belonia, Paikhola, Rajapur, Santirbazar, Baikhora, Jolaibari, Gardhang, Bhuratali, Manu Bazar, Kalachara, Sabroom, Baishnabpur, Dakshin Manu Bankul and Matai etc. in Cities and Adjoining areas of South Tripura District. b) Hotspot - The hot spot locations, capturing stationary user experience, are (i) Belonia Sub Post Office Bank Rd Opp. to Old Motor Stand Belonia; (ii) District Court Belonia; (iii) District Hospital Santirbazar; (iv) Iswar Chandra Vidyasagar College Belonia; (v) Jolaibari BDO Office Muhuripur R.F.; (vi) Manu H.S. School Manu Bazar; (vii) Sabroom Sub-Divisional Hospital Sabroom; (viii) The Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge Sabroom; (ix) Trishna Wild Life Sanctuary Belonia Joychandrapur. c) Walk Test - The walk tests conducted during 13 th to 15 th May 2026, covered (i) Sabroom Railway Station Paschim Jalefa and (ii) Sub-Division Hospital Belonia, capturing mobile network behaviour in crowded pedestrian environments. The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. title: Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis and Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol launch ‘Bharat Taxi’ service in Maharashtra
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis and Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol launch ‘Bharat Taxi’ service in Maharashtra Realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahakar Se Samriddhi’, ‘Bharat Taxi’, under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, is translating the cooperative model into action in the transportation sector ‘Bharat Taxi’ will create new employment opportunities for the youth, women and local sons of the soil of Maharashtra-Shri Murlidhar Mohol More and more youth should become ‘Sarathis of Cooperation’ and ‘Partners in a Prosperous Maharashtra’-Shri Murlidhar Mohol In ‘Bharat Taxi’, ‘Sarathis’ are not merely service providers but also owners and shareholders of the institution Bharat Taxi’s surge pricing-free and hidden charge-free system is providing affordable services to passengers and fair returns to Sarathis for their hard work The cooperative revolution initiated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and Union Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah has now reached Maharashtra’s transportation sector-Shri Devendra Fadnavis After Delhi and Gujarat, the launch of Bharat Taxi in Maharashtra will further advance this model of employment through cooperation and prosperity through employment प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi In a significant step towards transforming the country’s mobility sector through cooperation, innovation and inclusive development, Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis and Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol today launched the ‘Bharat Taxi’ service in Maharashtra at a programme held at Navi Mumbai International Airport. The initiative has been launched in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahakar Se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah. Several dignitaries, representatives of the cooperative sector, officials and Sarathis associated with Bharat Taxi were present on the occasion. Bharat Taxi is advancing an equitable cooperative mobility model that does not regard taxi Sarathis merely as drivers, but recognises them as owners of the service, members of the cooperative institution and partners in its progress. Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that the launch of ‘Bharat Taxi’ in Maharashtra marks the beginning of a new chapter in the State’s cooperative sector. He said that Maharashtra is the sacred land of cooperation and has a rich cooperative tradition spanning more than 100 years. Of the more than 8.60 lakh cooperative societies functioning across the country, nearly 2.5 lakh are operating in Maharashtra alone, reflecting the State’s significant contribution to India’s cooperative movement. Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi established a separate Ministry of Cooperation in 2021 with the objective of strengthening the country’s rural economy, extending the benefits of cooperation to every sector and ensuring the comprehensive development of cooperative institutions. He said that after Shri Amit Shah, who possesses extensive experience in the cooperative sector, was appointed the country’s first Minister of Cooperation, the cooperative movement received a new direction, fresh momentum and wider expansion. He added that the rural economy and the cooperative sector will play a significant role in realising the resolve of a developed India by 2047. The Union Minister of State for Cooperation said that, since the establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation, nearly 152 major decisions have been taken over the past five years to strengthen the cooperative sector. These include the new National Cooperation Policy, the target of establishing two lakh new multipurpose cooperative societies across the country and initiatives to make Primary Agricultural Credit Societies—PACS—economically viable. He informed that nearly 40,000 new cooperative societies have already been established. Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that PACS are being computerised at a cost of nearly ₹3,000 crore and have been enabled to undertake more than 25 types of economic and commercial activities. Nearly 39,000 cooperative societies across the country are operating Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras, while around 54,000 PACS are providing services as Common Service Centres. Cooperative institutions are now also operating petrol pumps and Jan Aushadhi Kendras and participating in grain storage and various rural service activities. These efforts are aimed at strengthening village-level cooperative institutions and thereby making farmers, villages, talukas, districts and States economically empowered and prosperous. He said that the Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited—BBSSL, National Cooperative Organics Limited—NCOL and National Cooperative Exports Limited—NCEL have been established to provide farmers with quality seeds, assured markets for organic products and export opportunities for agricultural produce. Nearly 70,000 cooperative institutions from across the country have become members of these three national cooperative organisations. The country’s first cooperative university has also been established to develop trained human resources for the cooperative sector. Referring to the steps taken under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis to strengthen Maharashtra’s cooperative sector, Shri Mohol said that financial assistance of nearly ₹10,000 crore has been provided to cooperative sugar mills in the State through the National Cooperative Development Corporation—NCDC. Activities related to ethanol and Compressed Biogas are also being promoted in the State. Important steps have also been taken towards creating an independent legal framework for the cooperative housing sector and promoting self-redevelopment. He said that Maharashtra has become the first State in the country to provide land for an initiative to promote tissue culture through cooperatives. The Union Minister of State for Cooperation said that, through Maharashtra’s extensive network of cooperative institutions and organisations, the Bharat Taxi service will be expanded to different parts of the State in the coming period. He urged the youth and women of the State to join Bharat Taxi in large numbers. He said that Bharat Taxi will create new employment and self-employment opportunities while making Sarathis partners in the progress and profits of the cooperative institution. He called upon people to become “Sarathis of Cooperation” and “Partners in a Prosperous Maharashtra”. Addressing the gathering, Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis said that the impact of the new revolution brought about in the cooperative sector under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the country’s first Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah is now visible in Maharashtra’s transportation sector as well. He said that, after Delhi and Gujarat, the launch of Bharat Taxi in Maharashtra will further advance the new model of employment through cooperation and prosperity through employment. From village-level primary cooperative societies to various cooperative organisations, efforts are being made to strengthen, modernise and bring greater transparency to these institutions, while also developing new business models for them. ‘Bharat Taxi’ is an important component of this transformative approach. Shri Devendra Fadnavis said that app-based taxi services have made transportation more convenient for passengers, but challenges such as surge pricing, hidden charges and aggregator commissions have often caused difficulties for both passengers and drivers. Bharat Taxi offers a cooperative solution to these issues. Under this model, taxi Sarathis will not merely be drivers but will also be owners and shareholders of the cooperative institution and will receive a share in the profits earned by it. The service will have no surge pricing or hidden charges and will operate on the basis of a fixed service fee. He said that ‘Bharat Taxi’ will provide citizens with safe, reliable and high-quality transportation services. The safety of women passengers, courteous treatment of passengers, transparent fares and an accountable service delivery system will be accorded priority. Referring to the agreement with the late D. B. Patil Cooperative Transport Association as significant, he said that efforts would be made to provide taxis through credit facilities to nearly 3,000 to 4,000 local sons of the soil residing around Navi Mumbai International Airport and connect them with the ‘Bharat Taxi’ platform. This will create new employment and entrepreneurship opportunities for local youth. During the programme, share certificates and service kits were also distributed to Sarathis associated with Bharat Taxi. Bharat Taxi aims to replace an intermediary-centric system with a Sarathi-centric transportation framework, bring stability to their incomes, provide passengers with safe services at transparent fares and share the institution’s profits with its Sarathis. In the coming period, the ‘Bharat Taxi’ service will be expanded across Maharashtra in a phased manner by connecting more taxi drivers, youth, women and local communities with the platform, in collaboration with the State’s cooperative institutions, transport organisations and local bodies. *** AK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288421) आगंतुक पटल  : 166 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Marathi , Gujarati Ministry of Cooperation Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis and Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol launch ‘Bharat Taxi’ service in Maharashtra Realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahakar Se Samriddhi’, ‘Bharat Taxi’, under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, is translating the cooperative model into action in the transportation sector ‘Bharat Taxi’ will create new employment opportunities for the youth, women and local sons of the soil of Maharashtra-Shri Murlidhar Mohol More and more youth should become ‘Sarathis of Cooperation’ and ‘Partners in a Prosperous Maharashtra’-Shri Murlidhar Mohol In ‘Bharat Taxi’, ‘Sarathis’ are not merely service providers but also owners and shareholders of the institution Bharat Taxi’s surge pricing-free and hidden charge-free system is providing affordable services to passengers and fair returns to Sarathis for their hard work The cooperative revolution initiated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and Union Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah has now reached Maharashtra’s transportation sector-Shri Devendra Fadnavis After Delhi and Gujarat, the launch of Bharat Taxi in Maharashtra will further advance this model of employment through cooperation and prosperity through employment प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that the launch of ‘Bharat Taxi’ in Maharashtra marks the beginning of a new chapter in the State’s cooperative sector. He said that Maharashtra is the sacred land of cooperation and has a rich cooperative tradition spanning more than 100 years. Of the more than 8.60 lakh cooperative societies functioning across the country, nearly 2.5 lakh are operating in Maharashtra alone, reflecting the State’s significant contribution to India’s cooperative movement. Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi established a separate Ministry of Cooperation in 2021 with the objective of strengthening the country’s rural economy, extending the benefits of cooperation to every sector and ensuring the comprehensive development of cooperative institutions. He said that after Shri Amit Shah, who possesses extensive experience in the cooperative sector, was appointed the country’s first Minister of Cooperation, the cooperative movement received a new direction, fresh momentum and wider expansion. He added that the rural economy and the cooperative sector will play a significant role in realising the resolve of a developed India by 2047. The Union Minister of State for Cooperation said that, since the establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation, nearly 152 major decisions have been taken over the past five years to strengthen the cooperative sector. These include the new National Cooperation Policy, the target of establishing two lakh new multipurpose cooperative societies across the country and initiatives to make Primary Agricultural Credit Societies—PACS—economically viable. He informed that nearly 40,000 new cooperative societies have already been established. Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that PACS are being computerised at a cost of nearly ₹3,000 crore and have been enabled to undertake more than 25 types of economic and commercial activities. Nearly 39,000 cooperative societies across the country are operating Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras, while around 54,000 PACS are providing services as Common Service Centres. Cooperative institutions are now also operating petrol pumps and Jan Aushadhi Kendras and participating in grain storage and various rural service activities. These efforts are aimed at strengthening village-level cooperative institutions and thereby making farmers, villages, talukas, districts and States economically empowered and prosperous. He said that the Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited—BBSSL, National Cooperative Organics Limited—NCOL and National Cooperative Exports Limited—NCEL have been established to provide farmers with quality seeds, assured markets for organic products and export opportunities for agricultural produce. Nearly 70,000 cooperative institutions from across the country have become members of these three national cooperative organisations. The country’s first cooperative university has also been established to develop trained human resources for the cooperative sector. Referring to the steps taken under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis to strengthen Maharashtra’s cooperative sector, Shri Mohol said that financial assistance of nearly ₹10,000 crore has been provided to cooperative sugar mills in the State through the National Cooperative Development Corporation—NCDC. Activities related to ethanol and Compressed Biogas are also being promoted in the State. Important steps have also been taken towards creating an independent legal framework for the cooperative housing sector and promoting self-redevelopment. He said that Maharashtra has become the first State in the country to provide land for an initiative to promote tissue culture through cooperatives. The Union Minister of State for Cooperation said that, through Maharashtra’s extensive network of cooperative institutions and organisations, the Bharat Taxi service will be expanded to different parts of the State in the coming period. He urged the youth and women of the State to join Bharat Taxi in large numbers. He said that Bharat Taxi will create new employment and self-employment opportunities while making Sarathis partners in the progress and profits of the cooperative institution. He called upon people to become “Sarathis of Cooperation” and “Partners in a Prosperous Maharashtra”. Addressing the gathering, Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis said that the impact of the new revolution brought about in the cooperative sector under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the country’s first Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah is now visible in Maharashtra’s transportation sector as well. He said that, after Delhi and Gujarat, the launch of Bharat Taxi in Maharashtra will further advance the new model of employment through cooperation and prosperity through employment. From village-level primary cooperative societies to various cooperative organisations, efforts are being made to strengthen, modernise and bring greater transparency to these institutions, while also developing new business models for them. ‘Bharat Taxi’ is an important component of this transformative approach. Shri Devendra Fadnavis said that app-based taxi services have made transportation more convenient for passengers, but challenges such as surge pricing, hidden charges and aggregator commissions have often caused difficulties for both passengers and drivers. Bharat Taxi offers a cooperative solution to these issues. Under this model, taxi Sarathis will not merely be drivers but will also be owners and shareholders of the cooperative institution and will receive a share in the profits earned by it. The service will have no surge pricing or hidden charges and will operate on the basis of a fixed service fee. He said that ‘Bharat Taxi’ will provide citizens with safe, reliable and high-quality transportation services. The safety of women passengers, courteous treatment of passengers, transparent fares and an accountable service delivery system will be accorded priority. Referring to the agreement with the late D. B. Patil Cooperative Transport Association as significant, he said that efforts would be made to provide taxis through credit facilities to nearly 3,000 to 4,000 local sons of the soil residing around Navi Mumbai International Airport and connect them with the ‘Bharat Taxi’ platform. This will create new employment and entrepreneurship opportunities for local youth. During the programme, share certificates and service kits were also distributed to Sarathis associated with Bharat Taxi. Bharat Taxi aims to replace an intermediary-centric system with a Sarathi-centric transportation framework, bring stability to their incomes, provide passengers with safe services at transparent fares and share the institution’s profits with its Sarathis. In the coming period, the ‘Bharat Taxi’ service will be expanded across Maharashtra in a phased manner by connecting more taxi drivers, youth, women and local communities with the platform, in collaboration with the State’s cooperative institutions, transport organisations and local bodies. *** AK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288421)

                23 JUL 2026 3:55PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Culture administers a number of schemes for the preservation, and promotion of India's tangible and intangible cultural heritage across the country, including in the States of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. For the promotion and conservation of tangible cultural heritage, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) is responsible for the protection and conservation of Centrally Protected Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains. In addition, the Ministry is implementing the Development of Excavation Sites and Heritage Complexes (DESH) Scheme, a Centrally Sponsored Sub-Scheme announced in the Union Budget 2026, for the promotion and sustainable development of 15 selected tangible cultural heritage sites across the country. The Ministry also implements the Museum Grant Scheme, under which financial assistance is provided for the development, modernization and digitization of museums at the regional, State and district levels. The State/UT-wise and year-wise details of funds allocated/sanctioned and utilized under the Museum Grant Scheme during the last three financial years, including for Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, are given atAnnexure-I. For the promotion and safeguarding of intangible cultural heritage, the Ministry implements the Scheme for Safeguarding the Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH), which supports the identification, documentation, preservation, safeguarding and promotion of India's living heritage. The Ministry also implements the Cultural Functions and Production Grant (CFPG) Scheme, under which financial assistance is provided for organizing cultural programmes, performances and production-based activities to promote regional, folk and classical art forms. Further, under the Financial Assistance for Promotion of Guru-Shishya Parampara (Repertory Grant) Scheme, financial assistance is provided to eminent gurus and their repertory groups to preserve, promote and transmit India's classical performing arts through the traditional guru-shishya tradition. These schemes are implemented under the Scheme for Promotion of Art and Culture, a component of the umbrella scheme Kala Sanskriti Vikas Yojana (KSVY). Budgetary allocation is made under KSVY and utilized for its various sub-schemes and components. title: DEVELOPMENT OF SPIRITUAL CORRIDORS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture DEVELOPMENT OF SPIRITUAL CORRIDORS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi The infrastructural and aesthetic development of the spiritual corridors in Kashi, Ayodhya and Mathura has been undertaken through tourism infrastructure projects sanctioned under various schemes of the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, including Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD), Swadesh Darshan, Swadesh Darshan 2.0, Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD), Assistance to Central Agencies (ACA) and Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI). These projects are sanctioned based on proposals received from the respective State Governments/ UT Administrations, subject to the prescribed scheme guidelines and availability of funds. The details of progress made in the development of these spiritual corridors are at Annexure. The projects have been designed to integrate modern visitor amenities while preserving the cultural, architectural and heritage character of these important spiritual destinations, thereby enhancing the overall pilgrimage experience. The tourism infrastructure developed under these schemes is also expected to generate positive socio-economic outcomes by promoting cultural tourism, increasing tourist footfall and creating additional livelihood opportunities for local artisans, tourist guides, and stakeholders in the hospitality and allied sectors. Further, to promote cleanliness, environmental sustainability and ecological balance around heavily visited heritage sites, the Ministry encourages States/UTs to incorporate sustainable components in the sanctioned projects, including solid waste management systems, sewage treatment facilities, public sanitation infrastructure, landscaping and plantation, rainwater harvesting, energy-efficient and solar lighting systems, eco-friendly mobility solutions and other environmentally responsible measures. This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra    Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. *** M Annadurai ANNEXURE THE DETAILS OF PROGRESS MADE IN INFRASTRUCTURAL AND AESTHETIC DEVELOPMENT OF SPIRITUAL CORRIDORS IN KASHI, AYODHYA AND MATHURA SL.                 23 JUL 2026 3:52PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Culture is implementing a digitisation initiative through the JATAN software, developed in technical collaboration with C-DAC, Pune, for digitisation of museum collections and archival resources. A national digital repository has been created through the Museums of India portal, where digitised collections of eight National Level Museums, two ASI Site Museums and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Museum, Pune are available. As on 15.07.2026, 3,75,707 artefacts out of 4,88,983 artefacts have been digitised and made available online (Annexure-I). Digitised Articles till date can be viewed by accessing the following link: https://museumsofindia.gov.in/repository Digitisation of collections and archival resources is also being undertaken in a phased manner by the Ministry and its organisations. Further, under the Museum Grant Scheme, financial assistance is provided for digitisation of museum collections. During the last three financial years, financial assistance of Rs.25 lakh has been sanctioned under the Scheme for this purpose. The Gyan Bharatam Mission, launched under the Ministry of Culture, aims to safeguard India’s vast manuscript heritage and revive its civilizational knowledge traditions for future generations. In this regard, more than 3.5 lakhs digitised manuscripts are available on Gyan Bharatam portal at present for public access which can be viewed by accessing the following link: https://gyanbharatam.com/ Digitisation of archival records are undertaken by the National Archives of India under the Ministry of Culture with the objective of preserving valuable documentary heritage and facilitating wider access to archival records. The National Archives of India is in the process to digitise 30 crore pages and preservation of 4.5 crore pages. The current status of project is as under- Total no. of digitised images as on 21.07.2026 is 17, 67, 40, 596 (Approx: 17.67 Cr) Public accessibility has been enhanced through the availability of digitised collections on digital platforms and by strengthening digital repositories and searchable databases. Also, the digitised archival records are being uploaded to NAI's dedicated portal, 'Abhilekh Patal', to facilitate worldwide access to India's archival heritage for researchers, scholars, and the general public. Statistics are available on the Abhilekh Patal portal at: https://www.abhilekh-patal.in/ This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today *** M Annadurai Annexure – I Comparative statement for digitised collections available on the website till 15 th July, 2026. title: ANCIENT MONUMENTS AND HERITAGE SITES IN SOUTH INDIA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture ANCIENT MONUMENTS AND HERITAGE SITES IN SOUTH INDIA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi There are 1100 monuments and sites (areas) declared as of national importance in South India, which are under the care and maintenance of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). The State-wise details are as under: Sl. No Name of State Number of Monuments and Sites 1. Andhra Pradesh 136 2. Karnataka 506 3. Kerala 30 4. Puducherry (UT) 07 5. Tamil Nadu 412 6. Telangana 09 Total 1100 Periodic inspections are carried out by ASI to assess the status of protected monuments and sites. Based on the requirement, works related to maintenance, preservation, restoration and conservation are taken up as a regular practice, in accordance with the National Conservation Policy, 2014, and subject to availability of resources. Further, no protected monument or site is in a deteriorating condition. The funds allocated and utilized during last five years on conservation of protected monuments and sites located in southern states under ASI is as follows: (Rupees in Crores) Financial Year Allocation Expenditure 2021-22 56.64 56.44 2022-23 94.48 94.48 2023-24 97.83 97.83 2024-25 67.48 67.44 2025-26 79.89 79.89 ASI promotes community participation and awareness through heritage walks, lectures, exhibitions, competitions, guided tours and outreach programmes organised on occasions such as World Heritage Day, World Tourism, and World Heritage Week etc. Further, to enhance tourism while ensuring preservation, ASI has provided visitor amenities like as drinking water, toilets, Braille signage, QR code-based information systems, souvenir shops, and sound and light shows etc. at selected monuments and sites with high visitor footfall. title: PROMOTING INDIAN CULTURE ABROAD
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture PROMOTING INDIAN CULTURE ABROAD प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 3:50PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Culture promotes India's art and culture abroad with a view to strengthening cultural relations with foreign countries through the conclusion and implementation of Cultural Agreements, Cultural Exchange Programmes, Memoranda of Understanding on Cultural Cooperation, and other bilateral cultural instruments. The Ministry also coordinates India's participation in multilateral cultural forums, including G20, BRICS, SCO, SAARC, and other international platforms, to enhance cultural cooperation and promote India's soft power. Further, the Ministry administers the Global Engagement Scheme (GES), under which Festivals of India are organised abroad to showcase India's diverse cultural traditions. The Scheme also provides Grants-in-Aid to Indo-Foreign Friendship Cultural Societies through Indian Missions abroad for the promotion of Indian art, culture, and cultural exchanges. The Scheme “Global Engagement Scheme” has been revised and continued for the period FY 2026-27 to 2030-31 with an outlay of Rs. 299.94 crore. The Scheme has the following Sub Schemes: International Cultural Exchange Programme Project Mausam Brihattar Bharat Safeguarding the Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) and Diverse Cultural Traditions of India In addition, the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), an organisation under the Ministry of External Affairs, plays a significant role in promoting Indian culture across the world through Indian Missions/Posts and its network of Cultural Centres abroad. ICCR undertakes a wide range of cultural activities, including the teaching of Yoga, Indian classical and folk dance, vocal and instrumental music, Indian languages and other cultural disciplines. title: Successful development of first indigenous Expendable Turbo Jet Engine of 350 kg thrust class
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence Successful development of first indigenous Expendable Turbo Jet Engine of 350 kg thrust class प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 8:19PM by PIB Delhi The first indigenous Expendable Turbo Jet Engine of 350 kg thrust class, designed by DRDO’s Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE), has been successfully developed. GTRE had identified Azad Engineering, Hyderabad as Industry partner for the manufacturing and assembly of the engine. On July 22, 2026, the engine was successfully realised and delivered to GTRE by Azad Engineering, a landmark achievement for India's aerospace and defence ecosystem. The delivery marks the culmination of years of precision engineering, advanced manufacturing, and close partnership between India's scientific & industrial communities. Mastered by only a handful of nations, jet engine technology is widely regarded as one of the most sophisticated engineering disciplines in the world, demanding exceptional precision, advanced metallurgy, and uncompromising manufacturing standards. Delivery of such complex system based on the design of DRDO reflects the growing technological capabilities of the Indian Defence Industry. The engine was handed over to Distinguished Scientist & Director General (Aeronautical Systems) Dr K Rajalakshmi Menon and Outstanding Scientist and Director GTRE Dr SV Ramanamurty by CEO Azad Engineering Shri Rakesh Chopdar. Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh complimented the partnership of GTRE and industry that has been instrumental in transforming the vision into a historic milestone. *** VK/ Savvy (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288576) आगंतुक पटल  : 56 Ministry of Defence Successful development of first indigenous Expendable Turbo Jet Engine of 350 kg thrust class प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: DRDO conducts successful maiden flight-test of ‘Kusha’ Long-Range Surface-to-Air Missile
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence DRDO conducts successful maiden flight-test of ‘Kusha’ Long-Range Surface-to-Air Missile प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO) successfully conducted the maiden flight-test of ‘Kusha’ Long-Range Surface-to-Air Missile from the APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the coast of Odisha on July 23, 2026. This maiden test was conducted against an electronic target simulating high-speed and high-altitude aerial threat which was successfully intercepted by the missile system. The ‘Kusha’ missile system is capable of neutralising a wide variety of aerial threats including fighter jets, missiles, unmanned aerial vehicles and large enemy aircraft within a wide range & altitude envelope. All weapon system elements, including the missiles, radars, command and control centre, have been developed by various DRDO laboratories and Industry partners. Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the successful test-flight of ‘Kusha’ marks an important milestone in Indian defence R&D, highlighting the capability in developing long range surface-to-air missile system, possessed only by a handful of nations. This, he added, will also eliminate the import dependency for such systems and signifies a giant leap in air defence capability of the nation. Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh monitored all activities during the launch and congratulated all the team members involved in the successful flight-test. title: OPERATION SOUTHERN READINESS 26-2 CONCLUDES AT SOUTHERN NAVAL COMMAND, KOCHI
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence OPERATION SOUTHERN READINESS 26-2 CONCLUDES AT SOUTHERN NAVAL COMMAND, KOCHI प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 7:25PM by PIB Delhi Operation Southern Readiness 26-2, a four-day multinational maritime security training engagement , concluded at Southern Naval Command, Kochi on 23 Jul 2026 . Conducted by the Indian Navy in partnership with Combined Maritime Forces (CMF) under the aegis of Southern Naval Command and the Indian Navy-led Combined Task Force 154 , the event brought together 276 personnel from 27 countries , supported by 76 facilitators and Subject Matter Experts, with participation from four international organisations. The engagement was inaugurated on 20 Jul 2026 by RAdm Deepak Singhal, Chief Staff Officer (Training), Headquarters Southern Naval Command, in the presence of Cmde Dan Thomas, Deputy Commander, Combined Maritime Forces, senior officers, and representatives of participating nations. The Closing Ceremony, held on 23 Jul 2026, featured a closing address by Cmde Milind M Mokashi, Commander CTF 154, presentation of certificates to the facilitators, and a valedictory address by the Chief Staff Officer (Training). The programme brought together maritime security, legal and operational perspectives through professional discussions, simulator-based instructions, and practical training. Sessions addressed Maritime Domain Awareness and Information Sharing, Maritime Law, Counter-Narcotics, Force Protection Measures, Asymmetric Threats, Maritime Uncrewed Systems, and Operational Sea Training. The domain-specific training was facilitated through inputs from the Indian Navy, including the Information Fusion Centre - Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR), CMF elements such as the Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC), and specialist international organisations including the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the IMO International Maritime Law Institute (IMO IMLI). Participants also undertook practical training in Damage Control and Firefighting, maritime communications, Survival at Sea, and Boarding procedures, besides sea training onboard Indian Naval ship. These activities provided opportunities for participants to exchange experiences and Best Practices, contributing to building greater understanding across maritime services and organisations. The engagement strengthened interoperability, professional networks, and operational confidence among participating nations. It also contributed to regional capacity-building and collective maritime security by combining theoretical understanding with hands-on training. The four-day engagement generated 3,800 training man-hours . Operation Southern Readiness 26-2 demonstrated the Indian Navy’s modern training infrastructure, state-of-the-art simulators, advanced instructional methodologies, and professional expertise . The successful conduct of the exercise has reinforced the Indian Navy-CMF partnership and has underscored Indian Navy’s leadership of CTF 154 whilst highlighting Southern Naval Command’s role as a leading training hub and preferred destination for professional maritime training. _____________________________________________________________ VM/AS                                                                                                       138/26 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288511) आगंतुक पटल  : 86 Ministry of Defence OPERATION SOUTHERN READINESS 26-2 CONCLUDES AT SOUTHERN NAVAL COMMAND, KOCHI प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: NEP 2020 is laying the foundation for an inclusive, skill-centric and future-ready education system – Union Minister of State for Education
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education NEP 2020 is laying the foundation for an inclusive, skill-centric and future-ready education system – Union Minister of State for Education Dr Sukanta Majumdar stresses on the importance of strengthening implementation of centrally sponsored schemes for achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 Two-day Conclave of State and UT Education Ministers concludes प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 8:19PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State for Education and Development of North Eastern Region, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, today highlighted the transformative role of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 in shaping an inclusive, skill-centric and future-ready education system. He was addressing the concluding session of the two-day Conclave of State and UT Education Ministers to review Centrally Sponsored Schemes of the Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Ministry of Education, at the ICAR–National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), New Delhi. Dr Majumdar emphasised on the need to address existing challenges through collaborative efforts between the Centre and the States and UTs to ensure that every child, teacher and school were empowered to realise their full potential. He reiterated that the effective implementation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes is essential to achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The Minister underscored the importance of PM POSHAN and Tithi Bhojan in improving the nutritional well-being of children, particularly those from marginalized communities. He called upon States and UTs to continue strengthening school education through coordinated efforts and sustained focus on quality, equity and inclusion. The second day of the Conclave focused on key components of Samagra Shiksha and PM POSHAN under the PRAGATI platform. The sessions featured presentations, followed by suggestions and inputs from education ministers and officials of States and UTs. An open-house discussion was also organized on strengthening the implementation of centrally sponsored schemes, sharing best practices, and improving learning outcomes in school education. The Conclave provided a valuable platform for the Centre and the States and UTs to share experiences, deliberate on implementation challenges and identify opportunities for further strengthening the delivery of centrally sponsored schemes. The deliberations reaffirmed the collective commitment towards ensuring equitable, inclusive and quality school education for every learner and accelerating progress towards Viksit Bharat 2047. Presentations were made on the PM SHRI scheme by Additional Secretary, DoSEL, Shri Dheeraj Sahu; on ULLAS by Additional Secretary, DoSEL, Ms. Archana Sharma Awasthi; on inclusive education by Economic Advisor, DoSEL, Ms. A. Srija; on skill education by Joint Secretary, DoSEL, Ms. Prachi Pandey; and on PM POSHAN by Joint Secretary, DoSEL, Shri Asheesh Joshi. Joint Secretary, DoSEL, Dr. Amarpreet Duggal and other senior officials of the Union Ministry of Education, also attended the Conclave. ***** RRTN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288577) आगंतुक पटल  : 15 Ministry of Education NEP 2020 is laying the foundation for an inclusive, skill-centric and future-ready education system – Union Minister of State for Education Dr Sukanta Majumdar stresses on the importance of strengthening implementation of centrally sponsored schemes for achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 Two-day Conclave of State and UT Education Ministers concludes प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: WEATHER FORECASTING AND EARLY WARNINGS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Earth Sciences PARLIAMENT QUESTION: WEATHER FORECASTING AND EARLY WARNINGS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 1:30PM by PIB Delhi The Mission Mausam was launched by the Honorable Prime Minister on 14 January 2025 with the goal of making the country, including Maharashtra, a 'Weather-ready and Climate-smart' nation. The objective of Mission Mausam is to strengthen various components of the Earth System observations, to realize Earth System approach to provide an early warning system, for seamless weather and climate services to all. The scheme seeks to exponentially enhance the country's weather and climate observations, understanding, modelling and forecasting, leading to better, more useful, accurate, and timely services. The key objectives of this Mission include: Developing cutting-edge weather surveillance technologies and systems. Implementing higher-resolution atmospheric observations with improved temporal and spatial sampling and coverage. Deploying next-generation radars, wind profilers, and satellites equipped with advanced instrument payloads. Implementing advanced high-performance computing (HPC) systems. Enhancing our understanding of weather and climate processes and improving prediction capabilities. Developing advanced Earth system models and data-driven methods, including the use of AI/ML Creating technologies and protocols for effective weather management Establishing a state-of-the-art Decision Support System (DSS) and dissemination system for last-mile connectivity Strengthening capacity building and research collaborations The current status of the observational network and modeling capability are as follows: India Meteorological Department (IMD) presently receives data from a network of 50 Doppler Weather Radars (DWRs) operated by IMD and other MoES institutions and ISRO across the country. The observational network is being progressively strengthened through the deployment of 29 C-Band DWRs, 45 X-Band DWRs, and 12 S-Band DWRs across the country to enhance weather monitoring observations, numerical weather prediction, and the study of atmospheric dynamics. These initiatives are expected to significantly improve the country's observational capabilities, including those in Maharashtra. The current DWR network in Maharashtra is given in Annexure-I. Under the Mission Mausam initiative, various global and regional Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) modeling systems have been implemented and operationalized to provide seamless short-range, medium-range, and extended-range weather forecasts, thereby further enhancing the accuracy and reliability of weather forecasting services. There are two different frameworks of global modeling systems based on global forecast systems (GFS) of IMD and Mithuna modeling systems of NCMRWF, Noida. Both models run in real-time with a horizontal resolution of 12 km. The New Bharat Forecasting System (BharatFS) is operational at a very high resolution of 6 km to cater to block levels and further to panchayat levels. In order to provide computational support for such high-resolution models and to make it regularly run in real time, the computing facilities have also been substantially increased with computational power to integrate voluminous data and to run mesoscale, regional, and global models at higher resolution. The "Arunika" supercomputing system at the National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF), Noida, and the "Arka" system at the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune, have significantly enhanced the Ministry of Earth Sciences' overall high-performance computing capacity. The Ministry of Earth Sciences has implemented various measures to strengthen disaster early warning systems for cyclones, heavy rainfall, and other extreme weather events across the country, including in Maharashtra. These measures are applicable across all seasons, including the ongoing southwest monsoon. The major initiatives are as follows: Augmentation of the observational network. Development of indigenous, technology-driven, and citizen-centric weather forecasting systems that strengthen disaster preparedness and improve public safety across India. IMD's in-house developed Decision Support System (DSS) is a major step in the direction of promoting self-reliance under the "Atmanirbhar Bharat" initiative. As a result, there is 40% improvement in forecast accuracy for all types of severe weather events in recent decades as compared to the previous decade. Impact-based forecasts and risk-based warnings are being disseminated at the district level, empowering authorities to take timely preventive actions against cyclones, heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, heatwaves, and cold waves. Developed "Mausamgram" (Har Har Mausam, Har Ghar Mausam), a unique citizen-focused platform providing location-specific, hyperlocal weather forecasts down to the village level. "Mausamgram" delivers hourly forecasts for the next 36 hours, three-hourly forecasts for the next five days, and six-hourly forecasts for up to ten days. Users can conveniently access weather information by searching through PIN code or location name, or by selecting the state, district, block, and gram panchayat. This user-friendly system ensures easy access to hyperlocal forecasts, enabling citizens to obtain accurate and timely weather updates tailored to their specific location. Development of climate hazard and vulnerability maps at the district level (https://imdpune.gov.in/hazardatlas/index.html) Development of geospatial services for weather forecast and warnings (https://imdgeospatial.imd.gov.in/) IMD is one of the agencies that generates Common Alert Protocol (CAP) alerts for severe weather warnings. These CAP alerts are disseminated through SMS as well as the SACHET app, developed by the NDMA. These CAP feeds are also being used by APPLE, GOOGLE, and GMAS for the dissemination of weather-related warnings. IMD has developed an Application Programming Interface (API), which is being used by various private and public organisations for further dissemination of IMD's forecasts and warnings to the general public through different media, including mobile apps developed by different stakeholders. IMD has developed various mobile apps for the dissemination of weather-related warnings, such as the MAUSAM App for weather forecasting and warnings, MEGHDOOT App for agro met services, DAMINI App for lightning warnings, and UMANG App for Weather forecasting and warnings. To enhance the local relevance and last-mile dissemination of weather information in remote and vulnerable regions, the India Meteorological Department, in coordination with other Ministries and stakeholders, has implemented the following major initiatives to support disaster preparedness during cyclones, heavy rainfall, and other extreme weather events. These initiatives are applicable across all seasons, including the ongoing southwest monsoon. In collaboration with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, IMD has developed the Panchayat Mausam Seva Portal, providing Panchayat-level weather forecasts through e-GramSwaraj (https://egramswaraj.gov.in), Meri Panchayat App, e-Manchitra, and Mausamgram (https://mausamgram.imd.gov.in). The mobile numbers of Panchayat Members, Ward Members, and Panchayat Secretaries have been integrated with the Panchayat Mausam Seva Portal, enabling the timely dissemination of weather forecasts and agrometeorological advisories through WhatsApp for further dissemination at the Gram Panchayat level. IMD also leverages the Krishi Sakhis and Pashu Sakhis network of the Ministry of Rural Development for last-mile dissemination of weather forecasts and agrometeorological advisories. IMD has organized over 7,300 Farmers' Awareness Programs (FAPs) across 373 districts, benefiting nearly 3.67 lakh farmers, including 83 Aspirational Districts, to promote climate-resilient agriculture and the effective use of weather-based advisory services. Under Mission Mausam, IMD has developed KALP (Krishi Advisory based on Location-specific Weather Prediction) for the generation of location-, crop- and crop-stage-specific advisories and Mausam SANKALP (Systematic Agrometeorological aNalytics, Knowledge and Advisory enabLing Platform) to strengthen weather analytics, advisory generation and climate-resilient agricultural planning. Timely alerts are transmitted in real-time to the Ministry of Home Affairs, the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs), District Magistrates, health departments, and public utility sectors. A direct, real-time coordination mechanism is maintained with District Collectors, SDMAs, the Department of Agriculture, and other local stakeholders to ensure rapid ground-level dissemination and administrative preparedness. Annexure-I Current operational DWR network in the State of Maharashtra: State DWR location-wise Maharashtra Mumbai (S-Band) Maharashtra Nagpur (S-Band) Maharashtra Solapur (C-Band) Maharashtra Veravali (C-Band) Maharashtra Mumbai, Juhu ( X-Band ) Maharashtra Mumbai, Panvel ( X-Band ) Maharashtra Mumbai, Vasai, Virar ( X-Band ) Maharashtra Mahabaleshwar ( X-Band ) Maharashtra Mumbai, Kalyan, Dombivali (X-Band) This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. ***** NKR/JKP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288239) आगंतुक पटल  : 309 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Earth Sciences PARLIAMENT QUESTION: WEATHER FORECASTING AND EARLY WARNINGS प्रविष्टि तिथि:

To ensure localised relevance and last-mile connectivity of weather updates in remote and vulnerable regions, IMD, in collaboration with other ministries, has undertaken the following major initiatives: In collaboration with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, IMD has developed the Panchayat Mausam Seva Portal, providing Panchayat-level weather forecasts through e-GramSwaraj (https://egramswaraj.gov.in), Meri Panchayat App, e-Manchitra, and Mausamgram (https://mausamgram.imd.gov.in). The mobile numbers of Panchayat Members, Ward Members, and Panchayat Secretaries have been integrated with the Panchayat Mausam Seva Portal, enabling the timely dissemination of weather forecasts and agrometeorological advisories through WhatsApp for further dissemination at the Gram Panchayat level. IMD also leverages the Krishi Sakhis and Pashu Sakhis network of the Ministry of Rural Development for last-mile dissemination of weather forecasts and agrometeorological advisories. IMD has organized over 7,300 Farmers' Awareness Programs (FAPs) across 373 districts, benefiting nearly 3.67 lakh farmers, including 83 Aspirational Districts, to promote climate-resilient agriculture and the effective use of weather-based advisory services. Under Mission Mausam, IMD has developed KALP (Krishi Advisory based on Location-specific Weather Prediction) for the generation of location-, crop- and crop-stage-specific advisories and Mausam SANKALP (Systematic Agrometeorological aNalytics, Knowledge and Advisory enabLing Platform) to strengthen weather analytics, advisory generation and climate-resilient agricultural planning. This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. ****** NKR/JKP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288238)

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: CAQM conducts Special Inspection of Urban Road Redevelopment works in Faridabad and Gurugram
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change CAQM conducts Special Inspection of Urban Road Redevelopment works in Faridabad and Gurugram Commission directs expediting Redevelopment Works and ensure Timely Completion in accordance with the prescribed Framework प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 7:44PM by PIB Delhi The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) conducted a special inspection drive in Faridabad and Gurugram on 22.07.2026. During the inspection, 64 road stretches spanning around 31 kilometres were assessed for compliance with the Commission's Standard Framework for Paving and Greening of Urban Roads. For the inspection drive, the Commission deployed 9 Flying Squads to inspect road stretches falling under the jurisdiction of the Municipal Corporation Faridabad (MCF) and the Municipal Corporation Gurugram (MCG). The inspection covered 50 road stretches under MCF and 14 road stretches under MCG. Roads falling under the Right of Way (RoW) categories of less than 10 metres and 10-15 metres were covered during the inspection. Of the 64 road stretches inspected, 49 road stretches (38 in Faridabad and 11 in Gurugram) were found to have end-to-end paving. However, end-to-end paving was not found on 15 road stretches, including 12 road stretches in Faridabad and 3 road stretches in Gurugram, indicating the need for completion of the remaining redevelopment works. The Commission also observed that although MCF and MCG claimed that the roads had been redeveloped in accordance with the Standard Framework, instances of non-compliance were detected during the inspection. The concerned agencies are being communicated to identify the officers/officials responsible for furnishing incorrect information to the Commission and to take appropriate disciplinary action against them. The Commission reiterated that such road stretches should be strictly and expeditiously (re)developed in accordance with the Standard Framework for Paving and Greening of Urban Roads. It emphasized that proper end-to-end paving of urban roads is one of the key measures for minimizing resuspension of road dust caused by vehicular movement and for enhancing the effectiveness of mechanized road sweeping and other dust mitigation measures. The concerned road-owning agencies have been advised to expedite the remaining redevelopment works and ensure timely completion in accordance with the prescribed Framework. The Commission further emphasized that implementation of the Standard Framework by all road-owning agencies across Delhi-NCR remains critical for long-term mitigation of road dust. Inspection drives will continue across NCR to monitor on-ground implementation of various air pollution control measures and facilitate timely corrective actions wherever required. ***** VM/GS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288531) आगंतुक पटल  : 40 Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change CAQM conducts Special Inspection of Urban Road Redevelopment works in Faridabad and Gurugram Commission directs expediting Redevelopment Works and ensure Timely Completion in accordance with the prescribed Framework प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PROGRESS OF LIFE MOVEMENT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PROGRESS OF LIFE MOVEMENT प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 4:22PM by PIB Delhi Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) is a mass movement aimed at nudging individuals and communities to practice an environment friendly lifestyle following a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society approach focusing on seven key themes viz., Save Energy, Save Water, Reduce Waste, Reduce E-Waste, Say No to Single Use Plastic, Adopt Healthy Lifestyles and Adopt Sustainable Food Systems. It aims at nudging citizens for bringing about behavioral change towards adopting a lifestyle that is in harmony with nature. The major activities undertaken under Mission LiFE since its launch in October, 2022 include the following: Nationwide mass mobilization campaigns, including One Nation One Mission: End Plastic Pollution, Harith Yoga, Swachhata Hi Seva, World Environment Day campaigns, Ideas4LiFE, e-waste awareness drives, and other outreach initiatives through the MyGov and MYBharat portals, have been undertaken by various stakeholders to promote awareness on Mission LiFE. Mission LiFE has been showcased through interactive digital exhibits at major national events like Bharat Parv, India Water Week, Maha Kumbh Mela, etc. Under the flagship "Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam" initiative over 272 Crore saplings have been planted. LiFE-Lifestyle for Environment included as one of the qualitative goals under India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement. The Ministry's EIACP Centres conduct awareness and capacity-building programmes on Mission LiFE themes. Further, over 12 lakh Eco-Clubs for Mission LiFE are working among children and youth in schools. Two dedicated digital platforms have been launched by the Ministry – the Mission LiFE Portal as a knowledge repository and the Meri LiFE Portal for structured reporting and monitoring of LiFE events and activities. So far, over 7.3 crore people participated in more than 40 Lakh LiFE events across the country which includes 31,49,967 participants participating in more than 2 lakh LiFE related awareness and action events in Maharashtra State. India's key international milestones include: At the Sixth Session of UNEA-6 held in Nairobi on 1 March 2024, India's resolution on "Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles", co-sponsored by Sri Lanka and Bolivia, was adopted unanimously. At the 15th Conference of the Parties (COP15) to the Ramsar Convention held in Zimbabwe on 30 July 2025, India's resolution on "Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles for the Wise Use of Wetlands" was adopted. India was elected to the Board of the 10-Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production Patterns (10YFP) for consecutive terms (2024–26 and 2026–28) and currently serves as Co-Chair, further strengthening the global agenda on sustainable lifestyles. Mission LiFE has been recognised in global forums like the Sharm-El-Sheikh Implementation Plan (COP27), the G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration, etc. India is steadily advancing towards achieving its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement. As per India's First Biennial Transparency Report (BTR-1) to the UNFCCC, the emissions intensity of GDP declined by 37.38% in 2022 compared to 2005. Forest and tree cover created an additional carbon sink of 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent between 2005 and 2022. India achieved over 50% of its cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil fuel sources, five years ahead of the 2030 target. Flagship initiatives include PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, the National Green Hydrogen Mission, National Nuclear Mission, Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) Programme. Further, to mobilise climate finance and accelerate low-carbon development, Sovereign Green Bonds and the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme have been introduced. Climate resilience is being strengthened through the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCCs). The abovementioned initiatives promote clean growth, energy security, industrial competitiveness, and climate resilience, supporting India's transition to a developed nation, thereby aligning with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 and India's commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2070. This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today. ***** VM/GS (Rajya Sabha US Q544) (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288318) आगंतुक पटल  : 129 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PROGRESS OF LIFE MOVEMENT प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT AT MOUNTAIN TOURIST SITES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT AT MOUNTAIN TOURIST SITES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, provide the statutory framework for environmentally sound management of solid waste in the country by respective State Governments / Urban & Rural local bodies / Bulk Waste Generators, as defined under the Rules. The rules inter-alia mandate four-stream segregation of solid waste at source into wet waste, dry waste, sanitary waste and special care waste and prescribe clear definition of bulk waste generators who have a mandate to fulfil Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility, in order to ensure that the waste generated is collected, transported and processed. The rules provide for the online tracking and monitoring of all stages of solid waste management through Centralised Online Portal including collection, transportation, processing and disposal. The rules have special provision for solid waste management in hilly areas and islands. The rules prescribe key role and responsibilities of State/UT Governments as well as Urban and Rural Local Bodies and Bulk Waste Generators in the implementation of the Rules. While State Governments are primarily responsible for sanitation, Swachh Bharat Mission Urban 2.0 (SBM U 2.0) and Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) [SBM (G)] provides central assistance to States / UTs for solid waste management in urban and rural areas of the country. Under Swachh Bharat Mission funds are allocated to Northeast States and Himalayan region States with fund sharing pattern of 90:10 between Centre and State, for solid waste management as per scheme Guidelines. ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: IMPACT OF NATIONAL CLEAN AIR PROGRAMME ON PM2.5 LEVELS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: IMPACT OF NATIONAL CLEAN AIR PROGRAMME ON PM2.5 LEVELS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi Pollution levels across countries are not directly comparable due to differences in geographical settings, weather conditions, and national circumstances. Air pollution is the collective result of multiple anthropogenic factors vehicular and industrial emissions, dust from construction & demolition activities, roads and open areas, burning of biomass and municipal solid waste, landfill fires and other dispersed sources compounded by adverse meteorological conditions. Government of India has notified the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for 12 air pollutants including PM10 and PM2.5 to safeguard public health and environment quality. To provide air quality information and associated health implications in an easily understandable manner, Air Quality Index (AQI) was launched by the Government in 2015. To address air pollution in urban areas in Mission mode, National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) was launched in 2019 by the Government in 130 Cities across the country which includes Pune, Surat, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Delhi. It is a multi-sectoral initiative involving the coordinated efforts of the Central and State Governments, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and other stakeholders. NCAP emphasizes source specific mitigation measures through city, state, and national-level clean air action plans and it is monitored by various committee constituted at Central, State and District level. State level Clean Air Action Plans prepared by States/UTs address both PM10 and PM2.5 through coordinated approach by implementing various policy and enforcement measures. Air quality performance based incentive grant of ₹ 16423.56 crore has been released to targeted cities under National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) as a critical gap funding to implement air pollution mitigation measures, during FY 2019-20 till 2025-26. To address air pollution in Delhi-NCR, Government has established the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) under the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas Act, 2021 for better coordination, research, identification and resolution of problems of air pollution in Delhi- NCR and adjoining areas. CAQM has been provided powers under the Act to take measures and issue directions to the various agencies in the National Capital Region for protecting and improving air quality. The focused and coordinated actions by 130 cities under NCAP have shown positive results with 108 cities recorded reductions in annual PM10 concentrations during 2025-26, compared to 2017-18, with 72 cities achieving reductions of more than 20% and 26 cities achieving reductions of more than 40%. Further, 14 cities met the National Ambient Air Quality Standards in FY 2025-26 (Standards ≤ 60 µg/m3), compared to six cities in 2017-18. Further, out of the 130 cities under NCAP, 65 cities have met the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for PM2.5 levels (Standard ≤ 40 µg/m³) in 2025-26. The PM2.5 level in Pune, Hyderabad, Surat, Delhi and Mumbai during 2025-26 was 41,34,32,102,33 µg/m³ respectively. This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today. ***** VM/GS (Rajya Sabha US Q545) (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288316) आगंतुक पटल  : 119 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: IMPACT OF NATIONAL CLEAN AIR PROGRAMME ON PM2.5 LEVELS प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT OF LANDFILLS IN DLEHI-NCR
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT OF LANDFILLS IN DLEHI-NCR प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 JUL 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has notified the Solid Waste Management Rules (SWM) Rules, 2026 in supersession of earlier SWM Rules, 2016 with provisions for proper and effective management of municipal solid waste (MSW), including sanitary landfills. The Rules have come into force with effect from 01.04.2026. The aforementioned Rules provide for establishment, construction, operation and maintenance of Sanitary Landfill by the concerned local body through eligible agencies. The Rules, also provide for responsibility of concerned District Magistrate to ensure operation of Sanitary Landfill as per provisions of the rules.
